name: Consumer Durables and Electronics

seo.title: Dealer Claims Reconciliation for Durables Brands | VipraTech
seo.description: Price protection, dealer incentives, co-marketing funds and warranty claims, checked against your terms and sales data for durables and electronics brands.

hero.headline: Settle price protection, incentives and warranty claims with every working shown
hero.subheadline: Price drops on dealer stock, sell-in and sell-out incentives, co-marketing funds and warranty repairs, checked before finance pays.

intro: Durables and electronics brands sell through distributors, large-format retailers and thousands of dealers, with frequent price changes and season-long incentive schemes. Each price drop creates price protection claims on dealer stock, each scheme ends with incentive calculations dealers dispute, and every repair under warranty is a claim from a service centre.

challenges.title: Frequent price drops
challenges.detail: Each price change triggers protection claims that depend on dealer stock on the day.

challenges.title: Complex incentives
challenges.detail: Sell-in and sell-out targets, model-mix conditions and festive schemes make payouts hard to check.

challenges.title: Shared marketing costs
challenges.detail: Dealers and retailers claim co-marketing funds with invoices and photos.

challenges.title: Warranty leakage
challenges.detail: Out-of-warranty, repeat and overcharged repairs are claimed by service centres.

use_cases.note: Price protection claims capped at the dealer stock that could have been held on the price-change date.
Sell-in, sell-out and festive incentives calculated from billing, returns and collections, with dealer statements.
Dealer and retailer co-marketing claims matched to approved activities and budgets.
Service-centre warranty claims checked against serial numbers, sale dates and rate cards.
Large-format retailer payments and debit notes checked against agreed margins and support.
Credit notes for protection, incentives and support matched to approvals and dealer ledgers.
Transit damage on large appliances and televisions, checked against POD remarks, with carrier recoveries.
Transporter bills for plant-to-warehouse and warehouse-to-dealer moves, checked against lane rates and PODs.
Early-payment discounts dealers take, checked against invoice dates and bank realisation.
Accessories, small appliances and electronics on quick-commerce platforms, with deductions checked against POs and GRNs.

documents: Price change circulars and dealer stock statements
Warranty job cards and serial records
systems: ERP such as SAP or Oracle

facts.text: Quick-commerce players are moving into higher-value categories such as electronics, beauty and gifting.

faqs.q: Dealers report their own stock for price protection. How do you check it?
faqs.a: Stock on the price-change date is estimated from what each dealer bought and sold, and from earlier stock reports. Claims above the estimate are flagged with the workings.
Yes, if sell-out or activation data is available, it can be used in the incentive rules.

faqs.q: Can it handle transit damage claims from dealers?
faqs.a: Yes. Damage claims are checked against LR and POD remarks, and losses the evidence places with the transporter go on a recovery sheet.
